Q: extracting a table from a pdf in which one column is half filled A:

Here's a shot at that table, starting with the "OFFICE_PRICE_INDEX.pdf" file you linked to. (Incidentally, if you're trying to get the file yourself, it appears to be geoip-fenced, so if you can vpn into Greece, that worked for me.)

Assumptions given the screenshot above:

  • we are interested in the "Total", "Athens", etc, in the top row; I will retain those and name 3rd and beyond columns with that context; you can grab the Greek names instead of English by changing the pattern in topcat
  • other than "year" and the bottom-half "period" (Η1/Η2, noting internally that that is not an ascii "H" in the PDF), all other columns are in groups of 3 for each of the meta-columns noted in the previous bullet
  • the ellipses "…" will be converted to NA
  • we are not interested in the plot at the bottom
  • where the year (column 1) alternates blank, ultimately we want to fill those down so they are not blank
  • I broke out the *-indicators to a new column "provisional"; this is as much to indicate provisional as it is to ensure year can be integer
txt <- pdftools::pdf_text("OFFICE_PRICE_INDEX.pdf") |>
  strsplit("[\r\n]+") |>
  .subset2(1)

topcat <- grep(" {4,}Total {4,}", txt, value = TRUE)
topcat <- strsplit(trimws(topcat), " {2,}")[[1]][-1]
topcat
# [1] "Total"          "Athens"         "Thessaloniki"   "Rest of Greece"

### first and last lines of the "table"
line_1n <- range(grep("^([12][0-9]{3}| +\\S[12]\\*? +[0-9.])", txt))
line_1n
# [1] 13 70
txt[line_1n]
# [1] "2006                                     …                         …                              …                     104.0                         …                        …                       …                         …                         …                       …                        …                          …"  
# [2] "2025                   H1*              97.7                         0.5                         4.8                    111.1                       0.9                        6.5                    86.5                      1.7                       6.5                     84.9                    -0.3                         2.0"

txtm <- strsplit(txt[line_1n[1]:line_1n[2]], " +")
maxlen <- max(lengths(txtm))
### each row has 13 or 14 strings, assuming those with 13 are
### missing the "period" (2nd) column; not checked here, but if there
### are more than two lengths of rows (13 and 14 here) then more care
### will be needed in this step to homogenize them into a matrix
dat <- t(sapply(txtm, function(x) {
  x <- if (length(x) < maxlen && grepl("^[0-9]+", x[1])) {
    c(x[1], "", x[-1])
  } else x
  ifelse(x == "…", NA, x)
})) |>
  `colnames<-`(c("year", "period", c(t(outer(topcat, c("_index", "_prevperiod", "_prevyear"), paste0))))) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(year = replace(year, !nzchar(year), NA_character_)) |>
  fill(year) |>
  mutate(
    provisional = grepl("*", year, fixed = TRUE) | grepl("*", period, fixed = TRUE),
    across(c(year, period), ~ sub("*", "", .x, fixed = TRUE)),
    across(everything(), ~ type.convert(.x, as.is = TRUE))
  ) |>
  relocate(provisional, .after = period)

Resulting in the top/bottom few rows looking like this:

dat[c(1:3, 54:58),]
# # A tibble: 8 × 15
#    year period provisional Total_index Total_prevperiod Total_prevyear Athens_index Athens_prevperiod Athens_prevyear Thessaloniki_index Thessaloniki_prevperiod Thessaloniki_prevyear `Rest of Greece_index` `Rest of Greece_prevperiod` `Rest of Greece_prevyear`
#   <int> <chr>  <lgl>             <dbl>            <dbl>          <dbl>        <dbl>             <dbl>           <dbl>              <dbl>                   <dbl>                 <dbl>                  <dbl>                       <dbl>                     <dbl>
# 1  2006 ""     FALSE              NA               NA             NA          104                NA              NA                 NA                      NA                    NA                     NA                          NA                        NA  
# 2  2007 ""     FALSE              NA               NA             NA          108.                4.2             4.2               NA                      NA                    NA                     NA                          NA                        NA  
# 3  2008 ""     FALSE              NA               NA             NA          112.                3.8             3.8               NA                      NA                    NA                     NA                          NA                        NA  
# 4  2023 "H1"   FALSE              89.9              3.1            7           98.6               1.6             7                 78.3                     2                     2.2                   82.4                         5.4                       8.1
# 5  2023 "Η2"   FALSE              91.4              1.7            4.8        102.                2.9             4.5               78.1                    -0.3                   1.7                   82.8                         0.5                       5.9
# 6  2024 "H1"   FALSE              93.2              2              3.7        104.                2.8             5.8               81.2                     4                     3.6                   83.2                         0.5                       1  
# 7  2024 "Η2"   TRUE               97.2              4.3            6.3        110.                5.6             8.6               85                       4.7                   8.9                   85.1                         2.3                       2.8
# 8  2025 "H1"   TRUE               97.7              0.5            4.8        111.                0.9             6.5               86.5                     1.7                   6.5                   84.9                        -0.3                       2

There is some fragility here:

  • I handle "*" (provisional data) and remove it before type-converting the data, but if there are other notes/superscripts attached to numbers in the table, then you'll need to add processing similar to what I did for provisional
  • I think I handled the non-ascii regex okay, but it is possible that unicode might trip up some of my logic
  • the determination of what lines from pdf_text() indicate data is fairly specific (in line_1n); since pdf can be problematic by sometimes returning leading space on some tables (not seen here), you may need to tweak the line_1n patterns so that "just the data" is extracted.
  • if they use blanks instead of ellispes (not seen here), then the sapply(..) portion will need a lot more logic to try to infer what should be blanks; if this is the case, looking at txt[line_1n[1]:line_1n[2]] one can see that fixed-width is an option, in which case an alternate approach using read.fwf() could also be used, though it is also not without some challenges

Q: Valgrind addresses vs Printf addresses in C A:

use the valgrind errors to track down misbehaving pointers

Whether you use valgrind or not, there is no guarantee whatsoever that two consecutive runs of the same program will produce the same pointer values. In my practice the values are not the same even for simplest programs, so comparing pointer values from different runs is meaningless.

If you for some reason need to relate pointers from different runs, you need to instrument your code yourself. One way to do so is to wrap your allocation functions, add a global call counter to them, and log pairs (call-counter, returned-pointer-address) to a file. Pointers with the same call-counter are the "same" pointer, provided that the program behaves deterministically and reads the same exact input.

Q: How do I stabilise Sort-Object in PowerShell 5.1? A:

You can achieve stable sorting by using 2 sorting expressions, very similar as in your answer just a bit shorter; the first expression sorts by odd numbers first, then by their value (ascending):

# This
1..20 | Sort-Object { $_ % 2 -eq 0 }, { $_ }

# Or this
1..20 | Sort-Object @{ Expression = { $_ % 2 }; Descending = $true }, { $_ }

Alternatively, using a single expression that creates a ValueTuple<bool, int> (comparable structure). This works very similar as the previous example just that we're combining the 2 sorting expressions (odd first, then value) into a single structure:

1..20 | Sort-Object { [System.ValueTuple[bool, int]]::new($_ % 2 -eq 0, $_) }

OrderBy and OrderByDescending from LINQ also perform stable sorting by default, so this works well in your case:

[System.Linq.Enumerable]::OrderByDescending(
    [int[]] (1..20),
    [System.Func[int, int]] { $args[0] % 2 })

A caveat is that if the incoming collection is not already ordered you might need to also apply ThenBy (to sort by value) or the ValueTuple<bool, int> example, in which case the simplest alternative is using Sort-Object.

[int[]] $collection = 1..20 | Sort-Object { Get-Random }

[System.Linq.Enumerable]::ThenBy(
    [System.Linq.Enumerable]::OrderByDescending(
        $collection,
        [System.Func[int, int]] { $args[0] % 2 }),
    [System.Func[int, int]] { $args[0] })

There are more ways to achieve the same stable sorting, for example using ValueTuple<bool, int>, a custom Comparer<int> and Array.Sort, honestly not worth using in PowerShell due to their complexity...

Q: How do I use executables, installed by a dependency package, in the dependent package? A:

In the context where generator expressions are accepted, full path to the imported executable can be referred via $<TARGET_FILE:tgt> expression (in your case tgt is foo:do_foo). There are also expressions for path portions, like directory (TARGET_FILE_DIR), basename (TARGET_FILE_NAME) and extension (TARGET_FILE_SUFFIX).

As first argument for the COMMAND clause in add_custom_command or add_custom_target instead of $<TARGET_FILE:tgt> expression you may just write the name of the target: CMake will automatically expand it to the full path.

Things become more complicated if you want to run executable during the configuration of the bar project, where generator expressions are not allowed. In that case you need to extract path from the target property IMPORTED_LOCATION. But take into account, that instead of that property the location could be specified via IMPORTED_LOCATION_<CONFIG> property; in that case you need to explicitely refer to a property from some configuration.
